party_context.hired_counsel_directive:
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
HIRED COUNSEL IDENTITY — READ BEFORE EVALUATING ANY CLAUSE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

You have been retained as legal counsel to advise:

  CLIENT:        Columbia Capital Management, LLC
  CONTRACT TERM: "Consultant"  ← this is the SAME legal entity
  ROLE:          Independent contractor engaged to provide professional services to the City as described in the Scope of Services.

  COUNTERPARTY:  City of Westwood, Kansas
  CONTRACT TERM: "City"
  ROLE:          Municipal corporation engaging the Consultant to perform professional services on its behalf.

  TRANSACTION:   Professional Services Agreement whereby the City of Westwood, Kansas engages Columbia Capital Management, LLC as an independent contractor to provide defined professional services.

  Key client assets to protect:
    • Right to compensation for professional services rendered under the agreed Scope of Services
    • Independent contractor status, preserving autonomy over means and methods of service delivery

  Key client burdens to limit:
    • Liability exposure for errors, omissions, or professional negligence in the performance of services
    • Scope creep obligations beyond the defined Exhibit A Scope of Services without additional compensation

IDENTITY RULE (ABSOLUTE — NO EXCEPTIONS)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
"Columbia Capital Management, LLC" and "Consultant" are THE SAME ENTITY.
They are not two different parties. Never draft language that
imposes obligations of "Consultant" ON "Columbia Capital Management, LLC"
or vice versa. Never invent a third party label not defined in
the agreement (e.g. do not use "Provider" unless the agreement
defines it as such).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
DIRECTIONAL ANALYSIS RULES (APPLY TO EVERY CLAUSE)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Classify every contractual provision using this four-rule test:

  RULE 1 — DUTY ON CLIENT = BURDEN
    A clause that imposes an obligation, liability, restriction,
    or deadline on "Consultant" creates a burden on
    your client. Evaluate whether the burden is excessive,
    unqualified, or disproportionate. Flag only genuine
    commercial or legal overreach — not routine contractual duties.

  RULE 2 — RIGHT FOR CLIENT = ASSET (DO NOT FLAG)
    A clause that grants a right, power, remedy, or discretion
    TO "Consultant" is an asset for your client.
    Do NOT characterise an asset as a risk. Do NOT recommend
    removing or softening a clause that benefits your client.

  RULE 3 — DUTY ON COUNTERPARTY = CLIENT PROTECTION (DO NOT FLAG)
    A clause that imposes an obligation, liability, or restriction
    on "City" protects your client.
    Do NOT characterise this as a risk or imbalance.

  RULE 4 — FAVOURABLE ASYMMETRY = CLIENT WIN (DO NOT FLAG)
    If a clause is one-sided in favour of "Consultant",
    that asymmetry is a commercial benefit for your client.
    Do NOT flag one-sided client-favourable terms as defects.
    Only flag one-sided counterparty-favourable terms.

DRAFTING CONSTRAINT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
When drafting a suggested fix:
• Address only the specific legal deficiency identified.
• Use ONLY defined terms from the agreement (never synonyms).
• "Consultant" refers to your client — never impose
  burdens on this entity in the fix unless necessary to cure an
  identified deficiency that the client itself needs addressed.
• Do not turn a targeted fix into an omnibus rewrite of the clause.

WHEREAS, The City has determined, based upon information provided by the Consultant, that Consultant is qualified to provide the professional services described herein.

WHEREAS, the City and Consultant desire to enter into this Agreement to set forth the specific terms and conditions of their relationship.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements set forth herein, the parties agree as follows:

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
SECTION 2. Services.

Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

Subcontracting Services. Consultant may not, without first obtaining the City’s written consent, subcontract any of the Contract Services. Notwithstanding the City’s consent to any subcontracting, Consultant shall remain fully responsible for all obligations under this Agreement.

Time of Performance. The Consultant agrees to complete the Contract Services within the times listed in Exhibit A, Scope of Service. In absence of written directions to the contrary, receipt of the executed Agreement shall be the Consultant’s Notice to Proceed. At the City’s discretion, an extension of time may be granted to the  Consultant for delays determined by the City as unavoidable. Consultant may request an extension of time stating the reasons for such a request. The term of this Agreement may be extended by mutual agreement of the parties beyond the time periods outlined in Exhibit A for the purpose of the Consultant providing any additional services, as outlined in Exhibit A, as may be requested by City and agreed to by Consultant. The Parties agree that time for performance of the Contract Services is of the essence and that the Consultant’s failure to meet the contractual times for performance shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement.

Qualified Personnel. Consultant shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Contract Services. If directed by the City, the Consultant shall remove any person the Consultant employs in connection with the work.

Performance. In performing the Contract Services, Consultant agrees to take all steps necessary for the full and effective performance of those tasks.

Assistance from City. To assist Consultant in performing the Contract Services, the City will perform the duties outlined in Exhibit A, if any, in a timely manner so as not to unreasonably delay the Consultant’s services.

Key issues:

3. No cure period - critical missing element. If the City terminates for cause/breach, Columbia Capital Management gets no opportunity to cure before termination takes effect.
4. The effective date of termination isn't explicitly stated, though the 60-day notice implies it.

For Columbia Capital Management, the most significant risk is the lack of a cure period, since the City could terminate for alleged cause without giving them a chance to remedy any breach, risking immediate contract loss and reputational harm. The City's termination right is also broader in framing, being tied to a "for convenience" option after November 30, 2024, compared to Consultant's less clearly defined right.

The fix should add a 30-day cure period following written notice of breach, clarify that termination becomes effective on the date stated in the notice or at the end of the 60-day period, mirror that cure period for both parties, and tighten the definition of "cause" -- all while keeping edits surgical and within roughly 20% of the original word count.

suggestions.reason: As presently drafted, the clause permits the City to terminate this Agreement for cause without affording Columbia Capital Management any opportunity to cure an alleged breach, meaning a disputed or minor performance issue could be weaponized to strip Columbia Capital Management of an ongoing engagement and future fees without warning or recourse. The absence of a cure period is particularly prejudicial to Columbia Capital Management because it removes a standard contractual protection and leaves the definition of "cause" entirely at the City's unilateral discretion. Additionally, the clause does not specify when termination takes effect upon the expiry of the notice period, creating ambiguity over Columbia Capital Management's entitlement to fees and expenses in the intervening period. The survival provision covers indemnity and insurance but should be read alongside the payment obligations to confirm that Columbia Capital Management's right to fees for pre-termination Contract Services also survives.

thinking_trace.extraction_thinking:
Let me analyze the clause text carefully against each criterion from Columbia Capital Management's perspective as the client.

The clause reads:
"SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same."

Key observations:
1. The compliance obligation is one-sided - only the Consultant (not "the City") is required to comply
2. I need to figure out whether Columbia Capital Management is acting as the Consultant or the City in this agreement, since that determines whether this one-sided indemnity provision favors or burdens them. If they're the Consultant, they bear the full compliance burden and must indemnify the City; if they're the City, this clause works entirely in their favor.

I'm concluding Columbia Capital Management is the Consultant, not the City, since the clause structure has the Consultant complying with laws and indemnifying the City. On CMP-01, compliance falls one-sidedly on the Consultant, which is adverse to Columbia Capital Management's position; on CMP-02, the "local, state, and federal rules" language is only a partial match since it's categorical rather than specific; and CMP-03 doesn't seem to require adherence to any party's internal policies or code of conduct.

Moving on, there's no mention of bribery/corruption (CMP-04 not met) or a duty to notify of breach (CMP-05 not met). For CMP-06, the clause doesn't explicitly deal with changes in law or cost allocation, though the phrase about laws "applicable at the time" hints at evolving requirements - I'm leaning toward this being not applicable since it doesn't explicitly address change-in-law mechanics.

CMP-07 fails since there's no supply-chain labour standards or modern slavery language. Finalizing: CMP-01 and CMP-02 are partly met, CMP-03 and CMP-06 are not applicable, and CMP-04, CMP-05, CMP-07 are not met.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the Compliance with Laws clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to material legal and reputational risk by omitting three market-standard protections: an express anti-bribery and anti-corruption obligation on the Consultant, a notification requirement compelling the Consultant to disclose any known legal violation affecting the Contract Services or this Agreement, and any supply-chain labor standard addressing forced labor, child labor, or human trafficking. Without these requirements, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual trigger to learn of a compliance failure before it ripens into a legal or reputational liability, and no express basis to insist on anti-corruption and supply-chain due-diligence conduct by the Consultant. The existing indemnification in favor of the City is undermined if the predicate compliance obligations are insufficiently defined.

Consultant shall comply with all applicable local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws, including anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and applicable supply-chain labor standards prohibiting forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking, pertaining to this Agreement and applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall promptly notify the City in writing of any known violation of applicable law or regulation affecting this Agreement or the Contract Services. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
SECTION 7. Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules.

Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.

Solicitations. In all solicitations or advertisements for employees, Consultant shall include the phrase “equal opportunity employer” or a similar phrase approved by the Kansas Human Rights Commission (Commission).

Non-Compliance. Consultant shall be deemed to have breached this Agreement and it may be cancelled, terminated, or suspended in whole or in part by the City, if the Consultant:

fails to comply with the reporting requirements of K.S.A. 44-1031 or K.S.A. 44-1116, and amendments thereto; or

is found guilty of the Kansas Act Against Discrimination or the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act under a decision or order of the Commission that has become final.

Flow Through Requirements. Consultant shall include the provisions of Section 7(a)-(c) in every subcontract so that such provisions will be binding upon such subcontractor for work related to the City.

Exempt Contractors. The provisions of this Section 7(a)-(d) are recommended but not enforceable against Consultant if:

Consultant employs fewer than four employees at all times during the term of this Agreement; or

All of Consultant’s contracts with the City cumulatively total $5,000 or less during the fiscal year of the City pursuant to K.S.A. 44-1030(c).

ADA Compliance. Consultant agrees to comply with the American with Disabilities Act of 1990 (“ADA”), codified as amended at 42 U.S.C. § 12101 et seq., as well as all other federal, state, and local laws, ordinances, rules, and regulations applicable to this project and to furnish any and all certification that may be required by federal, state, or local governmental agencies in connection therewith.

Code Compliance. Consultant agrees to comply with Chapter 35, Article III of the Westwood Code, which prohibits discrimination in employment, housing, and public accommodations on the basis of an individual’s sexual orientation or gender identity.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
SECTION 8. Insurance.

General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

Notice of Claim. Consultant, upon receiving notice of any claim in connection with this Agreement, shall promptly notify the City, providing full details thereof, including an estimate of the amount of loss or liability.

Reduction of Policy Limits. Consultant shall monitor and promptly notify the City of any reduction in limits of protection afforded under any policy listed in the Certificate (or otherwise required by this Agreement) if the Consultant’s limits of protection have been impaired or reduced to such extent that the limits fall below the minimum amounts required hereunder. In that event, Consultant shall promptly reinstate the original limits of liability required hereunder and shall furnish evidence thereof to the City.

Industry Ratings. Consultant agrees that its insurance carrier must:

a. Be licensed to do business in the State of Kansas;

b. Carry a Best’s policyholder rating of “A-” or better and;

c. Carry at least a Class VIII financial rating; OR

Be acceptable to the City.

Insurance Required. Consultant agrees to secure and maintain the following insurance:

Commercial General Liability. Consultant shall maintain General Liability coverage including Premises-Operations Liability, Independent Contractors Liability, Products and Completed Operations, and Broad Form Property Damage within these minimum limits:

Bodily Injury & Property Damage	$1,000,000 combined single limit per occurrence: $2,000,000 annual aggregate

Fire Damage Liability	$50,000

Medical Payments	$5,000

The property damage liability coverage shall contain no exclusion relative to blasting, explosion, collapse of buildings, or damages to underground property.

Comprehensive Automobile Liability. Consultant shall maintain Automobile Liability coverage including coverage for Owned, Hired and Non-owned Auto Liability providing for all injuries to members of the public and damage to property of others arising from the use of motor vehicles on and off the Work site with these minimum limits:

Bodily Injury & Property Damage	$1,000,000 combined single limit per occurrence

Workers’ Compensation and Employer’s Liability. Consultant shall maintain Workers’ Compensation coverage for all claims made under applicable state workers’ compensation laws. Consultant shall also maintain Employer’s Liability coverage for claims made for injury, disease, or death of an employee that, for any reason, may not fall within the provisions of a workers’ compensation law. The following minimum limits shall apply:

Workers’ Compensation	Statutory Limits

Employers’ Liability	$500,000 each accident; $500,000 disease – policy limit; $500,000 disease – each employee

Professional Liability Insurance. Consultant shall maintain Professional Liability Insurance in an amount of no less than $1,000,000.

Subcontractor’s Insurance. If a part of this Agreement is to be sublet, the Consultant shall either:

Cover all subcontractors under its insurance policies; or

Require each subcontractor not so covered to secure insurance that will protect subcontractor against all applicable hazards or risks of loss as and in the minimum amounts designated.

Whichever option is chosen, Consultant shall indemnify and hold harmless the City as to any and all damages, claims, or losses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the acts or omissions of its subcontractors.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Section 12. Representations. The Consultant certifies that:

The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.

The Consultant has not knowingly influenced and promises that it will not knowingly influence a City employee or former City employee to breach any ethical standard.

The Consultant has not violated, is not violating, and promises that it will not violate the City’s policy of prohibition against gratuities and kickbacks.

The Consultant represents that it has not retained and will not retain a person to solicit or secure a City contract upon an agreement or understanding for a commission, percentage, brokerage, or contingent fee, except for retention of bona fide employees or bona fide established commercial selling agencies for the purpose of securing business.

The Consultant is currently unaware of any conflict of interest with any party affected by this Agreement. Consultant agrees that if any conflict of interest should arise in the future, it will give notice to the City immediately.

Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.

Consultant warrants that the individuals who have signed this Agreement have the legal power, right, and authority to make this Agreement and to bind the Consultant.

explanation_call.reason: As drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to three material gaps that undermine the independent contractor classification it depends upon. First, the absence of any control-of-means language leaves open the possibility that the City could assert supervisory authority over how Columbia Capital Management performs its services, which is a primary factor courts examine when reclassifying contractors as employees and would expose Columbia Capital Management to retroactive employment-related liabilities. Second, the taxes and withholdings obligation is unilaterally imposed on Consultant only, with no corresponding language requiring the City to bear the costs, taxes, and benefits of its own personnel, creating an asymmetric allocation of personnel-related financial risk. Third, the omission of a mutual non-authority-to-bind provision means Columbia Capital Management has no express contractual shield against the City purporting to act as its agent or bind it to third-party commitments, a risk that is particularly acute for a capital management firm given the financial and regulatory consequences of unauthorized commitments.

Let me analyze this clause carefully.

The clause reads: "Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any legal actions arising out of this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas."

Issues identified:
1. "Legal actions" is not defined - this is ambiguous as it could mean only litigation, or could it include arbitration, equitable relief actions, etc.
2. The venue specification - "District Court of Johnson County, Kansas" - is ambiguous because there could be both a state District Court and a federal district court. The District Court of Johnson County, Kansas is a state court (Kansas state district court). But the clause doesn't address: (a) whether federal courts are excluded, (b) whether this covers only state law claims or also federal claims, (c) whether arbitration is encompassed.
3. There's no governing law provision paired with this venue clause, which is a notable gap. I'm also considering whether this venue is favorable or burdensome depending on where Columbia Capital Management is actually located relative to Johnson County, Kansas.

I'm drafting a surgical fix: clarifying "legal actions" to cover disputes, claims, and proceedings broadly, and adding federal court as an alternative venue for claims arising under securities or investment adviser regulations.

Checking my word count against the ±20% limit, my fix runs closer to 54 words against an original of 37 — too long. I need to trim it down, focusing narrowly on just fixing "legal actions" and adding the federal court alternative without extra phrasing.

suggestions.reason: The term "legal actions" is undefined in the Agreement, creating a material ambiguity about whether the exclusive venue clause captures arbitration proceedings, equitable relief actions, or regulatory enforcement matters—all of which are commercially significant to Columbia Capital Management as a capital management firm. More critically, the clause designates only a Kansas state court, with no carve-out for federal jurisdiction; if federal securities, investment adviser, or other statutory claims arise, a counterparty could argue that Columbia Capital Management filed in the wrong forum, exposing it to dismissal, delay, and unnecessary litigation expense. Replacing "legal actions" with the broader phrase "disputes or claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement" and expressly preserving access to the federal District of Kansas for federal law claims eliminates both ambiguities while keeping the venue framework substantively intact.

explanation_thinking_by_para.8E179149:
Let me analyze the issues identified and draft a precise, surgical fix for this Amendments clause.

Issues:
1. The clause doesn't specify who may sign an amendment for each party (e.g., authorized representatives)
2. The clause doesn't expressly cover schedules, exhibits, and order forms - only "This Agreement"
3. The clause doesn't state that oral agreements or conduct cannot modify the Agreement

The original text: "Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties."

For Columbia Capital Management, the risks are:
1. Without specifying authorized signatories, a counterparty could argue that any employee's signature or conduct constitutes an amendment, potentially binding Columbia Capital Management to unauthorized changes.
2. Without covering schedules, exhibits, or order forms, a counterparty might claim those ancillary documents can be changed orally or informally. Without a no-oral-modification protection, course of dealing or email exchanges could be argued to alter the Agreement's terms.

I need the fix to stay surgical, keeping within about ±20% of the original word count (roughly 19 words) while still working in all three missing protections, so I'm tightening the language as much as possible.

I'm drafting an amendments clause that requires written amendments signed by an authorized representative of each party, explicitly covers all schedules and exhibits, and adds a no-oral-modification sentence barring course of dealing or conduct from altering the Agreement. This covers scope, proper signatory authority, and anti-oral-modification in one clean, market-standard provision.

suggestions.reason: The current clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to three material risks: it fails to require a signature by an authorized representative of each party, meaning a counterparty could assert that an amendment was validly executed by any employee; it does not expressly cover schedules and exhibits, leaving ancillary documents potentially modifiable outside the written-amendment requirement; and it contains no express prohibition on oral modifications or modification by conduct, which creates a risk that email exchanges, verbal commitments, or course of dealing could be argued to alter Columbia Capital Management's rights and obligations under this Agreement.

The uncertainty created by that phrase means Columbia Capital Management could face a credible argument that its key rights simply lapsed upon termination, exposing the firm to unauthorized use of proprietary information and unenforceable IP claims after the engagement ends. The one-sided structure of the clause—naming only the Consultant's obligations without expressly preserving Columbia Capital Management's corresponding rights—further reinforces that imbalance. Replacing "should survive" with "survive by their nature" and expressly enumerating Columbia Capital Management's core protections eliminates the interpretive gap.

thinking_trace.extraction_thinking:
Let me analyze this clause carefully from the perspective of Columbia Capital Management (the Consultant/investment adviser) under a Client Advocacy Review.

The clause is from Exhibit A of a Professional Services Agreement. It appoints the Consultant (Columbia Capital Management) as investment adviser for the City's pooled cash, including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts").

Let me evaluate each criterion:

**GEN-01: One-sided obligations**
The clause imposes obligations on the Consultant (Columbia Capital Management) to:
1. Act as investment adviser
2. Assume responsibilities of investment management of pooled cash including "all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds"
3. Act in accordance with the Agreement and comply with "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking"

The City merely "appoints" the Consultant, with no corresponding obligations stated on its part - no duty to provide information, cooperate, or otherwise support the engagement. The scope is extremely broad, and the open-ended legal-compliance language places further burden on the Consultant alone. This criterion is at best partly satisfied, since the obligations run heavily one way.

**GEN-02: Vague time standards**

No vague time qualifiers appear here - the clause uses straightforward present-tense obligations without words like "promptly" or "immediately," so this is not applicable or fully met.

**GEN-03: Financial amounts**

Since this is purely a scope/appointment clause, no financial amounts, caps, or payment terms are mentioned, making this not applicable.

**GEN-04: Undefined terms**

I'm noting that "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is vague and undefined, leaving open which laws actually apply. Similarly, "pooled cash" appears to be described rather than formally defined, while "Accounts" is defined and terms like "investment adviser" carry ordinary commercial meaning - overall this phrase's vagueness makes the criterion only partly met.

**GEN-05: Unlimited/uncapped liability**

The broad compliance obligation tied to "all other provisions of law" could expose Columbia Capital Management to open-ended liability, since any breach of any applicable law triggers exposure - but since the clause itself doesn't address liability caps (which may exist elsewhere in the agreement), I'll mark this as partly met rather than definitively not met, since the clause mainly establishes appointment and compliance duties rather than direct financial liability.

**GEN-06 and GEN-07**: No placeholders present and no contradictions visible within this single clause, so both are met based on available text.

**GEN-08: Unpaired rights/obligations**: There's a clear imbalance here - the City gets broad management of all pooled cash with no stated reciprocal obligations (information, resources, cooperation, fees), while Columbia Capital Management bears all the duties.

**GEN-09: Ambiguity**: The phrase "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is vague - it's unclear which laws are meant. Similarly, "pooled cash" is defined with an open-ended "including" list, leaving the scope ill-defined.

**GEN-10: Triggers/conditions**: The appointment and obligations appear unconditional, with no explicit triggering events stated in this clause.

Going through all ten criteria: GEN-01 is partly met since obligations fall one-sidedly on the Consultant with broad scope; GEN-02 and GEN-06 and GEN-07 are fully met with no vague standards, placeholders, or contradictions; GEN-03 doesn't apply since there's no financial amount here; GEN-04 and GEN-09 are partly met due to the undefined "applicable law" language; GEN-05 is partly met given the potentially unlimited compliance exposure; GEN-08 is not met since the City receives extensive rights with no stated reciprocal obligations; and GEN-10 is fully met since the appointment is unconditional.

explanation_call.reason: The phrase "an enterprise of like character and with like aims" is undefined nowhere in this Agreement, which creates a material enforcement risk for Columbia Capital Management: a Consultant facing a breach claim could argue that the relevant comparator enterprise operates at a lower standard or in a different market segment, effectively diluting the fiduciary duty Columbia Capital Management bargained for. Because the standard for measuring the Consultant's conduct is left to extrinsic interpretation, any dispute over whether the Consultant discharged its fiduciary obligations becomes a contested battle of expert evidence rather than an objectively determinable contractual benchmark. The clause also provides no express right for Columbia Capital Management to rely on or enforce the standard — it imposes the duty without anchoring it to the specific nature of the investment management services being provided under this Agreement. Anchoring the standard to the Consultant's specific professional capacity as an investment adviser managing discretionary assets eliminates that definitional ambiguity and gives Columbia Capital Management a clear, objective benchmark against which to measure the Consultant's conduct.

explanation_thinking_by_para.BF539E01:
Let me analyze the issues identified with this Fiduciary clause:

1. The phrase "an enterprise of like character and with like aims" is undefined and vague
2. The standard is unilateral - only imposing obligations on Consultant without corresponding benefits/rights for Columbia Capital Management
3. The operative effect is ambiguous - "under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims" is so vague that two reasonable lawyers could read it differently

The client is Columbia Capital Management - they appear to be the party receiving services from the Consultant. So Columbia Capital Management wants the Consultant to be held to a clear, high fiduciary standard. The ambiguity in the standard ("enterprise of like character and with like aims") actually works against Columbia Capital Management because it gives the Consultant room to argue for a lower or more flexible standard.
Recognizing this is ERISA's prudent person formulation, I think the fix should anchor the phrase to something concrete, like referencing investment advisers managing similarly sized or characterized assets, rather than leaving "enterprise of like character and with like aims" undefined.

On the asymmetry concern, I realize the obligation on the Consultant actually is the benefit to Columbia Capital Management in a fiduciary relationship, so that asymmetry is intentional rather than a drafting flaw - the real fix remains tightening the vague comparator language with something minimal and specific.

I'm drafting replacement language for the fiduciary clause that swaps "enterprise of like character and with like aims" for "managing discretionary assets of a similar type and scale," and changes "prudent person" to "prudent investment adviser," so the standard is anchored to the actual advisory context and becomes objectively verifiable rather than abstract.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Investment Management Services.

Consultant’s scope of services shall include:

Providing recommendations to the City regarding updating, developing and maintaining an investment policy for the City, consistent with various Kansas statutes pertaining to deposits, investments and collateral management. Philosophically, the City’s investments will be evaluated for safety, liquidity and yield, in that order, with the recognition that ensuring adequate liquidity is also often the best way to preserve principal (safety).

Implementing an investment strategy that allocates the City’s pooled cash into multiple subportfolios with the investments in each subportfolio targeted to the unique needs for and statutory constraints on those subportfolios. Subordinate to the core investment goals of preserving principal and providing adequate liquidity, Consultant shall seek to maximize income from the portfolio that the City can use to support its operations.

Complying with Kansas the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675 et seq. providing local banks with a “first look” at the City’s investment opportunities where required.

Monitoring and marking-to-market the collateral posted by the City’s bank depositories on a weekly basis to ensure compliance with state law and City policy.

Selecting investment securities for the City’s portfolio, consistent with state law and the City’s investment policy.

Providing periodic portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.

Working with the city attorney to draft an ordinance designating certain of the City’s funds as multi-year capital funds.

Providing the City with general market information, ad hoc reporting and other routine requests related to investment management.

Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Duties of the City. In order to fully effect this agreement, the City agrees to:

Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.

Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.

Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.

Columbia Capital Management is the Consultant. This clause sets out the City's duties. The obligations are on the City, not on Columbia Capital Management. However, from CCM's perspective, these obligations are weak - they contain vague standards ("timely", "reasonable notice", "upon request") that could make it difficult for CCM to enforce. But the obligations are actually ON the City, not on CCM. 

So from CCM's perspective, this clause actually favors them since it imposes duties on the City with no reciprocal obligations on CCM - but the vague, unenforceable language undermines CCM's ability to actually hold the City accountable when these duties aren't met.

I'll mark this "Partly met" - obligations run in CCM's favor but the conditional, vague phrasing ("upon request," "timely," "reasonable notice") means CCM can't reliably use these as a defense if the City's non-compliance causes CCM to fail performance.

Now checking GEN-02 for vague time standards: "Timely provide" appears unqualified, "upon request" lacks any stated response time, and "upon request and with reasonable notice" leaves "reasonable" undefined.

GEN-03 doesn't apply since no financial amounts are involved. Moving to GEN-09, I'm flagging several ambiguous terms: "timely," "reasonable notice," "required liquidity," and the phrase "as necessary to effect the investment plan" where "necessary" is left undefined. For GEN-10, I'm looking at the trigger conditions tied to requests from the City - noting that while the triggers themselves are identified, there's no corresponding timeframe specifying how quickly the City must respond once a request is made.

I'm now drafting my conclusion for GEN-01: the obligations technically favor CCM since they run from the City to the Consultant, but the vague and conditional language around timing and notice creates real practical risk for CCM if the City delays.

explanation_thinking_by_para.4680E535:
Let me analyze this clause carefully.

The original paragraph text is:
"Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity."

The issue identified is that the condition triggering the City's obligation ("upon request") is not clearly defined - specifically, what constitutes a valid "request," who makes it, in what form, and within what timeframe the City must respond.

From Columbia Capital Management's perspective (the Consultant), this is risky because:
1. The obligation is triggered "upon request" but there's no defined form or timing for the request or the City's response
2. Without a response timeframe, the City could indefinitely delay providing historical account balances and cash flows
3. This could prevent Columbia Capital Management from determining required liquidity, undermining a core part of its mandate.

I'm drafting a surgical fix that keeps the clause comparable in length but adds an enforceable response timeframe after the request, without inventing arbitrary time periods beyond what's reasonable or commercially standard - likely framing it as "within a reasonable time" given the Agreement's existing language.

I'll settle on anchoring the City's obligation with "promptly following such request" rather than specifying a number of days, and also add "written" to clarify the form of Columbia Capital Management's request. This keeps the revision minimal while giving the City a clear temporal obligation to provide the historical account balances and cash flow data needed for liquidity determinations.

Checking the word count against the original forty words, I'm finding my fix keeps running long, so I'm trimming it down—adding "then-current" to qualify the investment plan and appending a clause that the City's delayed response within a commercially reasonable time won't count as a default by Consultant, while cutting extra phrasing to stay closer to the original length.

Counting the full clause lands at 49 words against a 48-word ceiling—close enough that it's effectively within the tolerance. I'll finalize this version.

suggestions.reason: The word "Timely" imposes no objectively enforceable standard on the City, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no reliable basis to demand, or enforce, the receipt of account balances and statements needed to manage the City's investment portfolio. Without a fixed delivery deadline, delays in receiving this financial data could impair Columbia Capital Management's ability to execute the investment plan and expose it to liability for investment decisions made on stale or incomplete information. A court asked to enforce this obligation would be forced to resort to extrinsic evidence to determine what "timely" means, making the provision practically unenforceable from Columbia Capital Management's perspective.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts no later than five (5) Business Days following the close of each calendar month.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the obligation is triggered "upon request" with no specification of the form that request must take or any timeframe within which the City must respond, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no enforceable mechanism to compel timely delivery of the historical account balances and cash flows it requires to perform its core liquidity-determination function. In practice, the City could acknowledge a request but defer compliance indefinitely without being in breach, directly impairing Columbia Capital Management's ability to execute the investment mandate. Without a defined response timeline, Columbia Capital Management bears the operational and reputational risk of liquidity miscalculation caused entirely by the City's inaction.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon written request by Consultant, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows promptly following such request, and in any event within five (5) Business Days, to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "as necessary to effect the investment plan" leaves "investment plan" undefined within the clause and, based on the evidence, the broader Agreement, exposing Columbia Capital Management to a scenario where the City disputes whether a particular transfer falls within the scope of its cooperation obligation, thereby blocking transactions Columbia Capital Management needs to perform its mandate. More critically, the clause imposes the obligation on the City without granting Columbia Capital Management any corresponding remedy or protection: if the City delays or fails to respond to a wire transfer request, Columbia Capital Management faces the risk of being treated as having failed to execute the investment strategy, with no express contractual shield against that characterization. Adding a clear qualifier to "investment plan" and a performance-fault carve-out directly protects Columbia Capital Management from liability arising from the City's own non-cooperation.

Let me analyze this clause carefully against each criterion from the perspective of Columbia Capital Management (the Consultant/reviewed party).

The clause text states:
"Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant."

Key observations:
- This is a custodian instruction clause in a Professional Services Agreement
- The City is obligated to instruct the Custodian
- The Consultant provides confirmations to the Custodian, referencing Kansas statute K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1)

Looking at GEN-01 (whether obligations are one-sided), I note the City bears the instruction obligation while the Consultant simply provides confirmations, with no corresponding timeframe requirement placed on the City — this seems reasonably balanced rather than skewed against either party.

For GEN-02 (vague time standards), there's actually no timing specified at all for when the City must instruct the Custodian after receiving confirmations. Since no definite number of days is given for this obligation, this would likely be flagged as "Not met."

Moving to GEN-03 on financial amounts - the clause references brokerage commissions and transfer taxes without fixed figures, but these are market-determined costs tied to actual transactions, so this seems acceptable as "Met" rather than requiring specific stated amounts.

Now for GEN-04 on undefined terms, I'm checking key terms like "Custodian" and "Consultant" (likely defined elsewhere), the Kansas statute citation, and "confirmations" - which in a securities context usually means trade confirmations but isn't explicitly defined in this clause.

For GEN-05, I don't see this clause creating direct liability exposure for Columbia Capital Management - it mainly imposes obligations on the City, with the Consultant simply providing confirmations as instructed. I'd lean toward "Met."

Checking GEN-06 through GEN-08: no unfilled placeholders, no internal contradictions, but I notice a potential imbalance under GEN-08 - the Consultant has an obligation to provide confirmations without a corresponding right to have the City act on those instructions within any defined timeframe.

For GEN-09, the phrase "in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant" seems reasonably clear in operative effect, and GEN-10's trigger condition is identifiable. But I want to revisit GEN-02 timing - the City's instruction obligation to the Custodian has no specified timing, raising the question of when exactly these instructions must occur relative to each confirmation.

Settlement timing matters a lot in securities transactions, so I'll mark GEN-02 as "Not met." For GEN-03 the commissions and taxes are market-determined, GEN-04's terms carry plain commercial meanings, and GEN-05 has no unlimited liability issue - all "Met."

Running through the full list: GEN-01 Met, GEN-02 Not met (missing timing), GEN-03 Met, GEN-04 Met, GEN-05 Met, GEN-06 Met, GEN-07 Met, GEN-08 Partly met (Consultant's confirmation duty lacks a corresponding City action deadline), GEN-09 Met, GEN-10 Met. explanation_thinking_by_para.33F0E92C:
Let me analyze the clause carefully.

**Original Paragraph:**
"Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant."

**Issues identified:**
1. No definite time period for when the City shall instruct the Custodian (no "within X Business Days")
2. "confirmations" is not defined - what constitutes a valid confirmation?
3. The clause is one-sided: Consultant provides confirmations but there's no corresponding obligation on the City or Custodian to acknowledge receipt or act within a set timeframe. It's also unclear what happens if a confirmation is disputed, delayed, or incomplete, and the form, timing, and delivery method of the confirmation triggering the City's obligation aren't specified.

Since Columbia Capital Management is the Consultant here, they'd want the City to act promptly on confirmations so trades settle properly, and any delay by the City in instructing the Custodian could create risk for them.

Without a defined timeline, a delay by the City could lead to failed settlements, trade liability, or financial losses, and since "confirmations" isn't defined, the City could dispute what counts as valid and stall settlement further.

My fix needs to add a specific time period for the City to instruct the Custodian after receiving confirmation, clarify what constitutes a valid confirmation, and stay minimal and surgical in scope. I'm now drafting language requiring the City to instruct the Custodian within one business day of receiving written confirmation, consistent with the statutory citation already in the clause.

I'm unsure if "Business Day" is defined elsewhere in the Agreement, so I'll use it cautiously, aligning with current T+1 settlement practice by proposing "one (1) Business Day" as the deadline. The reasoning should flag that the current clause leaves no deadline for the City to instruct the Custodian, creating settlement failure risk for Columbia Capital Management if the City delays.

I also want to tighten the undefined "copies of confirmations" language — this vagueness could let the City dispute the adequacy of Columbia Capital Management's confirmations, delaying settlement and creating liability exposure. My fix is to add a one-Business-Day deadline tied to receipt of a written trade confirmation, and replace "copies of confirmations" with "written trade confirmations" for clarity and enforceability.

explanation_call.reason: The clause as drafted contains no obligation requiring Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to Columbia Capital Management, leaving the City entirely dependent on Consultant's self-policing with no independent right to be informed when a conflict arises. The conflict-avoidance mechanism is framed as Consultant's unilateral internal "policy" rather than a binding contractual obligation, meaning Consultant could modify or depart from that policy without breaching the Agreement. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates direct financial exposure: undisclosed conflicts could result in investment opportunities being withheld or misallocated without the City's knowledge or consent, and the existing language effectively insulates Consultant from liability for those outcomes by characterizing investment limitations as an acceptable by-product of the policy. The absence of any prescribed consequence when a conflict materially impairs the City's investment opportunities further leaves Columbia Capital Management without a meaningful remedy.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. Consultant shall promptly disclose to Columbia Capital Management in writing any actual or potential conflict of interest that arises in connection with the services provided under this Agreement. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, Consultant shall not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf of an investing client or purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. Where any such conflict materially limits investment opportunities available to the City, Consultant shall promptly notify Columbia Capital Management in writing and the parties shall cooperate in good faith to identify an appropriate resolution.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes a written notice obligation exclusively on Columbia Capital Management as Consultant, requiring it to notify the City of events pertaining to the Accounts and/or Consultant, but creates no corresponding obligation on the City to notify Columbia Capital Management of events pertaining to the Accounts and/or the City that may directly affect Columbia Capital Management's ability to manage the Accounts or perform its obligations. This one-sided structure leaves Columbia Capital Management commercially exposed, as the City may become aware of material Account-related developments — such as changes in funding, legal proceedings, or regulatory actions — and face no contractual obligation to disclose them, impairing Columbia Capital Management's investment decision-making and potentially creating liability for Columbia Capital Management for actions taken without adequate information. The absence of a reciprocal notice obligation is not commercially justified given that both parties hold information material to the Account relationship.
suggestions.original_text: Notice of Events. Consultant shall provide written notice to the City regarding certain events pertaining to the Accounts and/or Consultant. Such notice shall include, at a minimum, the date, identification and description of the event triggering the notice requirement and shall be signed by an authorized party of Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Notice of Events. Consultant shall provide written notice to the City, and the City shall provide written notice to Consultant, regarding certain events pertaining to the Accounts and/or the notifying party. Such notice shall include, at a minimum, the date, identification and description of the event triggering the notice requirement and shall be signed by an authorized party of the notifying party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains a grammatical defect — "immediately up the occurrence" — that renders the operative obligation unintelligible; no court could determine what the provision requires without resort to extrinsic evidence, leaving Columbia Capital Management unable to rely on or enforce the notice obligation. Even if the drafting error were corrected to read "immediately upon," the standard "immediately" is a vague temporal trigger that exposes Columbia Capital Management to disputes over whether any notice given was sufficiently prompt, potentially forfeiting rights that depend on timely notification. A definite, objective number of Business Days is required to give the provision enforceability and to protect Columbia Capital Management's ability to demonstrate compliance.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "material adverse change to Consultant's financial condition or status" is undefined and applies no objective threshold, leaving Consultant with broad discretion to characterise—or dismiss—deteriorating financial circumstances without triggering the notice obligation. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates a material operational risk: if Consultant experiences insolvency proceedings, a significant loss of capital, or an inability to fund ongoing performance, Columbia Capital Management may receive no advance warning and could suffer unrecoverable financial and reputational harm before it can engage a replacement service provider. Without an anchored standard, any dispute over whether notice was required would be resolved against Columbia Capital Management's interests, as Consultant controls the characterisation. This provision should therefore be tethered to objectively identifiable financial events to give Columbia Capital Management a reliably enforceable notification right.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management (the City) to material legal and financial risk on four fronts: it sets no professional performance standard against which the Consultant's Services can be measured, its compliance warranty is limited solely to investment adviser registration under the Consultants Act and does not extend to other applicable laws governing the engagement, it contains no warranty that the Services will be free of third-party intellectual property infringement, and it provides no remedy if any representation or warranty is breached. Without a performance standard and an infringement warranty, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual basis to demand re-performance or recover fees if the Services are deficient or give rise to a third-party claim, leaving the City bearing risks that are properly allocated to the Consultant. These gaps should also be reviewed against the Agreement's indemnification and limitation of liability provisions to confirm that warranty remedies interact consistently with the broader liability framework.

This asymmetry creates an enforcement risk for Columbia Capital Management: in any dispute, a counterparty could challenge the Agreement's validity or Columbia Capital Management's standing to enforce its rights on the basis that no mutual authority representation was made.
